excerpt: You can create a Linux machine using the Paperspace console, Paperspace API, or Paperspace CLI.
You can connect to your Linux or Windows-based machine using the Paperspace console or desktop app using SSH connection.
Custom templates are templates of your machines and their configurations. You can use these custom templates to create new machines with your specifications.
Shared drives provide storage that is accessible from multiple machines in a private network.
The auto-shutdown feature places your machine in a stop state after a predefined period of inactivity, which can range from one hour to one week.
API keys let you interact with Paperspace through the Core RESTful API, the Core JavaScript SDK, and Gradient command-line utility (CLI).
Notebooks are a web-based Jupyter IDE with shared persistent storage for long-term development and inter-notebook collaboration, backed by accelerated compute.
Deployments are containers-as-a-service that let you run container images and serve machine learning models.
Workflows automate machine learning tasks, combining GPU instances with an expressive syntax to generate production-ready machine learning pipelines with a few lines of code.

The gaming community also used Paperspace sometimes for PC game streaming, allowing users to install Steam or other clients to tap into existing libraries. Worked pretty well for playing Assassin's Creed Odyssey on vacation.

Paperspace gives free access to Graphcore IPU nodes (4 IPUs each), theoretically more throughput than Colab T4. But porting Stable Diffusion web UI hit a wall needing an SDK upgrade behind a corporate login. Left a bad taste.
Paperspace locked me out of my account (froze it) but happily charged me. Didn't notice for a while since I didn't use it much. Support just ignored my questions.
Back in college Paperspace gave us a few thousand dollars in compute credits for our autonomous driving research project to help with training costs.

I use Stable Diffusion with Paperspace's Pro tier ($9/mo) for up to 6 hours of non per-usage GPU time, avoiding worry about electricity costs. Worried the plan might be replaced with strict per-usage pricing.
PaperSpace product recently has been really bad. Gradient Notebooks are a worse version of Google Colab, useless for serious DL product building.

Their DL virtual servers (Core) are horrible - very slow internet, takes forever to copy datasets in. Getting SSH access is an uphill battle; instead there's a pointless virtual console and confusing GUI. Once I found Lambda and Vast.ai, I never looked back.
I use a Paperspace VM + Parsec for personal ML projects. An hourly rate on a standard VM w/GPU is better than buying a local machine, and you can reuse these VMs for hobby gaming too.
Man I had such a problem using paper space's notebook system that I just gave up. In retrospect it was more to do with me not understanding generator functions to control memory bloating.
paper space has such an oddball product - they first started off as some sort of cloud Virtual Desktop type of thing and this seems to be their new pivot [into AI].
